memory_update.text: MOD has explicit data-center cooling exposure supported by annual-report evidence and Airedale by Modine product announcements; keep as a stronger underfollowed cooling candidate but verify revenue mix, backlog, capacity, and liquid-cooling share.

NVT maps to AI data-center liquid cooling, racks, power distribution, and connection products; evidence includes data-solutions materials and liquid-cooling product launch, but organic growth and customer materiality need filing-level verification.

CLS has one of the cleanest explicit relationships in this chunk to AI/cloud data-center infrastructure through CCS products including switches, optical systems, racks, servers, and storage for AI workloads.
IESC has strong underfollowed services exposure: fiscal 2025 filings cite data-center demand, record Communications backlog, and Q1 FY2026 revenue growth driven by data centers.
SMTC maps to 1.6T AI data-center optics via PMD, VCSEL driver, TIA, and optical/copper connectivity; next work should quantify revenue and design-win durability.

SANM relationship upgraded from hypothesis to fact for cloud/AI infrastructure manufacturing because fiscal 2025 materials cite ZT Systems data-center infrastructure manufacturing acquisition and cloud/AI infrastructure end-market strength.
VICR remains a plausible rack/board power candidate, but gathered evidence only proves exposure to enterprise/HPC and network infrastructure markets, not specific AI accelerator platform wins.
BELFB remains a messy-label component hypothesis; evidence supports power/protection/connectivity segments but not yet direct AI data-center content, customer wins, or component content per rack.

ATKR has data-center construction-component relevance through conduit/fittings/cable-management products, but AI-specific materiality is unproven and pricing/commodity cyclicality must be checked before it survives later layers.
APG has broad inspection/service/monitoring evidence but lacks explicit gathered proof of data-center or AI-data-center revenue; keep only as a low-confidence facility-services hypothesis.

PWR should remain a reference anchor for grid interconnection and transmission rather than the main underfollowed alpha lane; evidence supports data-center customer power opportunities but the company is already high-attention and large-cap.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the power, cooling, EMS/integration, electrical-infrastructure, and facility-services candidate chunk. Strongest relationship evidence in this chunk is for MOD, NVT, CLS, IESC, SMTC, and SANM because company filings or releases explicitly reference data centers, AI infrastructure, hyperscalers, liquid cooling, optical interconnect, or cloud/AI infrastructure. VICR, BELFB, ATKR, APG, and PWR remain useful supply-chain relationships but need sharper verification of AI-specific revenue, backlog, customer wins, and margin durability. PWR is retained as a reference anchor rather than an underfollowed discovery candidate.
